topic: What a mutex guarantees, starting from zero.
goal: State the mutual-exclusion guarantee and what it does not promise.
grill: I have never used a mutex and I want the real guarantee.
I write threaded Python on the homelab.
I do not want to guess.

facts.claim: A thread is an execution context inside a process.
Threads in one process share memory.
A mutex guarantees mutual exclusion: at most one thread holds it, so the protected section never runs concurrently.
